findings.evidence: AC13 requires `grep -ci 'every kit'` to print 0 for docs/handoff/PRIVACY.md. Line 30 of the current file reads '- Logging is off for every kit until an adult confirms that consent is in hand for each child in that group.' None of the 4.5 edits touches that line, and INV3 makes every other line byte-identical. So after a correct implementation AC13 prints 1 and fails. The implementer then has to break INV3, rewriting a consent sentence, or ignore a failing check. Also, a threat model that quotes that PRIVACY sentence would fail the same way.
findings.fix: Make AC13 test the claim itself, not the phrase. For example, check that no line containing 'alert' also contains 'every kit' (`grep -i 'alert' <file> | grep -ci 'every kit'` prints 0) in PRIVACY.md and docs/threat-model.md, together with the existing positive grep for 'Live stuck alerts for kits with logging off'. Or require a count of exactly 1 for PRIVACY.md, as line 30's baseline.

findings.evidence: AC9's script splits each Mitigation cell on ';' and requires every clause to name a jade- id. It also requires every id named there to appear in the Phase cell after 'Phase N'. Several planned cells put ';' inside parentheses: AB2 '(jade-fd5, jade-o07; ADR 0011)', AB5 '(jade-5nj, jade-zg3; ADR 0008, CLAUDE.md rule 3)', AB9 '(jade-6cq; ADR 0020)', AB14 '(jade-fd5; ADR 0011)', AB4 and AB12 '(the bead filed in 5.8 under the Phase 7 epic jade-7s7; phase to be confirmed, Q7)'. Each of these yields a clause with no id, such as 'ADR 0011)' or 'phase to be confirmed, Q7)'. In AB4 and AB12, jade-7s7 is also named in the Mitigation cell but not in the Phase cell. Only AB11's first clause is exempted, so the check as written reports failures on six rows of the plan's own text.
findings.fix: Split only on ';' outside parentheses, or use ',' inside the parenthetical citations. In AB4 and AB12, replace the epic reference in the Mitigation cell with the filed bead id (the parent link is already checked separately), or exempt epic ids from the Phase-cell match.

findings.evidence: D2 inserts into DATA-MODEL.md: 'Live stuck alerts (ADR 0017) have no table. The app holds them in memory per class until resolved or the session closes; they are never written to the database or logs.' This applies to all kits. The R1 fix limits P2 and the ALERTS node to kits with logging off and leaves the logging-on path open (Q3). If Q3 settles that a logging-on kit's alert comes from ingested `stuck` events, which are stored in `events`, D2 is false. That is the same over-claim R1 fixed in PRIVACY.md, now in DATA-MODEL.md. INV6 forbids picking an answer to an open question.
findings.fix: Limit D2 to match P2: 'Live stuck alerts for kits with logging off (ADR 0017) have no table... (whether kits with logging on use the same store is open, Q3).'
